newsitem.title: USA: Cash crudes slide with NYMEX, bullish factors ease.
newsitem.headline: Cash crudes slide with NYMEX, bullish factors ease.

text.p: U.S. cash crude prices slipped sharply from Friday morning as outright values declined in sympathy with NYMEX losses after short-term bullish buying evaporated.
Traders said the fact Colombian Cano Limon production returned Friday, and the lack of any major supply disruptions from Hurricane Danny deflated outright crude prices.
August West Texas Intermediate/Cushing was around 55 cents weaker at $19.35-45 a barrel, and held a 12 cents discount to the September WTI/Cushing.
Hurricane Danny forced Chevron to shut its 295,000 barrels per day refinery in Pascagoula, Mississippi as a precaution. No other major refineries were reported shut.
The second "bullish" prong underpinning the market was removed after Occidental Petroleum Corp said it resumed pumping along the Cano Limon-Covenas pipeline.
The pipeline was closed for the better part of two weeks after leftist rebels bombed the structure, forcing Occidental to declare force majeure on Cano field output.
Grade business saw West Texas Sour/Midland barrels sell at a $1.18 discount to the August benchmark, with deals only quietly moving.
"It looks like there is just some ratable barrel buying and not much else pushing the market," said a trader.
Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James was around a 20-25 cents premium to the marker, while Midland/WTI barrels hovered around last deals at 22 cents under the August WTI/Cushing.
